description: Completed 13 March 1943 and accepted by the Army 19 March 1943; a trainer at Parks Air College in Illinois then Perrin Army Air Field in Texas; surplus 1944 and sold 1945; bought by Butler County Warbirds in May 2000 and restored to flying condition in 2007; airworthy and used for public flight experiences but organisation-owned and kept in the City Hangar; no civil registration is published anywhere so the tail number carries the USAAF serial only

Built at the Aeronca factory in Middletown Ohio on 24 December 1941 a few miles from where it is now displayed; sold to a civilian then bought by the Defense Plant Corporation in 1942 and impressed as a tandem trainer with the Army Air Corps for only eleven months; sat in a barn near Peoria Illinois for around thirty years before being acquired September 1994 and restored to flying condition; no civil registration published
aliases: Grasshopper; Defender; c/n C2801TA; L3; L3E

description: Accepted by the Navy as an N2S-1 on 21 December 1940; served at three naval air stations and removed from Navy service 30 September 1944; the published N2S-1 Bureau Number blocks do not obviously contain 3240 so this figure taken from the organisation's own aircraft page should be checked against a BuNo card before being trusted; the Boeing construction number 75-1017 is consistent with an early Model 75
aliases: PT-17; Kaydet; Stearman; Model 75; c/n 75-1017; BuNo 3240; PT17

description: The only airframe ever to carry the XUC-86A designation; built as a Fairchild 24 with a 175 hp engine at Drew Field and later fitted with a 200 hp Ranger L-440 C-5; under restoration by staff and volunteers with a two-year timeline quoted in July 2021 so it is very likely still in pieces; no civil registration published
aliases: UC-86; Fairchild 24; Forwarder; c/n R9-422; XUC86; XUC86A; UC86
